title: Taxmin va ehtimollik ifodalash
goal_uz: Dars oxirida must have, might have, can’t have, probably, likely va bound to yordamida dalilga tayanib taxmin qilasiz va ishonch darajasini aniq ifodalaysiz.

scenes.title: Taxmin va ehtimollik
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda munozara va qarshi fikr bildirishni o‘rgandik. Bugun biz hali bilmagan narsalar haqida aqlli taxmin qilishni o‘rganamiz: “u kasal bo‘lsa kerak”, “u kechikkan bo‘lishi mumkin”, “u bunday qilgan bo‘lishi mumkin emas”. Dars oxirida siz rasm va vaziyatlar haqida ishonch darajasini aniq ifodalab gapira olasiz.
scenes.say: Hello again. Last time we practised debating. Today you will learn to speculate: to say what is probably true, what might be true, and what simply cannot be true. By the end, you will match your language to exactly how sure you are.
scenes.say_uz: Yana salom. Oldingi darsda munozara qildik. Bugun taxmin qilishni o‘rganamiz: nima ehtimol to‘g‘ri, nima mumkin va nima mutlaqo bo‘lishi mumkin emas. Oxirida til darajangizni ishonchingizga moslay olasiz.

scenes.title: Hozirgi vaqt: must, might, can’t
board: must be = I’m almost sure it is
might / may / could be = it’s possible
can’t be = I’m sure it isn’t

examples.t: He must be tired. He worked all night.
examples.uz: U charchagan bo‘lsa kerak. U tun bo‘yi ishladi.

examples.t: That can’t be Tom. He’s in Paris.
examples.uz: Bu Tom bo‘lishi mumkin emas. U Parijda.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi mavzu. Hozirgi vaqt haqidagi taxmin uchun modal fe’l va oddiy fe’l shakli ishlatiladi. “Must be” — deyarli aniqman, shunday. “Might be”, “may be”, “could be” — ehtimol. “Can’t be” — aniqman, bunday emas. Diqqat: “mustn’t” bu yerda ishlamaydi. “Must” ning inkori taxminda “can’t” bo‘ladi: “That can’t be Tom”.
scenes.say: Use modals to speculate about the present. He must be tired: I am almost sure. He might be at home: it's possible. That can't be Tom: I am sure it isn't. Notice that the opposite of must is can't, not mustn't.
scenes.say_uz: Hozirgi haqida taxmin uchun modal fe’l ishlating. U charchagan bo‘lsa kerak: deyarli aniqman. U uyda bo‘lishi mumkin: ehtimol. Bu Tom bo‘lishi mumkin emas: aniqman. Must ning teskarisi can't, mustn't emas.

scenes.title: O‘tgan vaqt: must have, might have
board: must have + V3 = almost sure it happened
might / may / could have + V3 = possible
can’t / couldn’t have + V3 = sure it didn’t

examples.t: She must have missed the bus.
examples.uz: U avtobusga kech qolgan bo‘lsa kerak.

examples.t: They might have forgotten the date.
He can’t have left yet. His coat is here.
examples.uz: U hali ketgan bo‘lishi mumkin emas. Paltosi shu yerda.

scenes.say_native: O‘tmish haqidagi taxmin uchun modal fe’l, “have” va fe’lning uchinchi shakli keladi. “Must have missed” — o‘tkazib yuborgan bo‘lsa kerak. “Might have forgotten” — unutgan bo‘lishi mumkin. “Can’t have left” — ketgan bo‘lishi mumkin emas. Bu ingliz tilining eng foydali tuzilmalaridan biri, chunki o‘tgan voqeani ko‘rmay turib, belgilar asosida baho beramiz.
scenes.say: For past events, use a modal plus have plus the past participle. She must have missed the bus. They might have forgotten the date. He can't have left yet. His coat is here. We judge what happened from the evidence we have now.
scenes.say_uz: O‘tmish uchun modal, have va uchinchi shakl. U avtobusga kech qolgan bo‘lsa kerak. Ular sanani unutgan bo‘lishi mumkin. U hali ketgan bo‘lishi mumkin emas, paltosi shu yerda. Biz hozirgi belgilarga qarab baho beramiz.

scenes.title: Davomiy va inkor shakllar

examples.t: He must have been working late.
She might not have heard the phone.

scenes.say_native: Jarayonni taxmin qilsak, “must have been working” deymiz: ishlab o‘tirgan bo‘lsa kerak. Inkorda ikki xil ma’no bor. “Might not have heard” — eshitmagan bo‘lishi mumkin, bu ehtimol. “Can’t have” yoki “couldn’t have heard” — eshitgan bo‘lishi mumkin emas, bu aniqlik.
scenes.say: For an action in progress, use must have been plus V-ing: He must have been working late. For negatives, there is a big difference. She might not have heard the phone means it is possible. She can't have heard it means I am sure she didn't.
scenes.say_uz: Jarayon uchun must have been va -ing: u kechgacha ishlayotgan bo‘lsa kerak. Inkorda katta farq: might not have heard — eshitmagan bo‘lishi mumkin. Can't have heard — eshitgan bo‘lishi mumkin emas.

scenes.title: Could have: ikki ma’no
board: He could have missed the bus. (taxmin)
can’t / couldn’t have = sure it didn’t

examples.t: She could have taken a taxi.
You could have told me!

scenes.say_native: “Could have” ikki ma’noga ega. Taxminda u “might have” ga teng: “She could have taken a taxi” — taksi olgan bo‘lishi mumkin. Ikkinchi ma’no — o‘tmishdagi imkoniyat, ya’ni qilinmagan ish: “You could have told me!” — menga aytishingiz mumkin edi, lekin aytmadingiz. Qaysi ma’no ekanini kontekst va ohang ko‘rsatadi.
scenes.say: Could have has two meanings. As a guess it equals might have: She could have taken a taxi. It can also mean a missed chance: You could have told me! Context and tone tell you which one is meant.
scenes.say_uz: Could have ikki ma’noda: taxmin, u might have ga teng. Yoki qo‘ldan boy berilgan imkoniyat: menga aytishingiz mumkin edi! Kontekst va ohang farqlaydi.

scenes.title: O‘zbekcha va ruscha bilan solishtirish
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida taxmin qo‘shimchalar bilan beriladi: “kelgan bo‘lsa kerak”, “kelgan bo‘lishi mumkin”, “kelgan bo‘lishi mumkin emas”. Inglizchada esa buning o‘rniga modal fe’l ishlatiladi: must have come, might have come, can’t have come. Ruscha «должно быть» ham “must be” ga to‘g‘ri keladi.
scenes.say: In Uzbek, speculation is built with endings and short phrases. In English, a modal does the work. Compare: You must go, which is an obligation, and You must be tired, which is a deduction.
scenes.say_uz: O‘zbekchada taxmin qo‘shimcha va iboralar bilan beriladi, inglizchada modal fe’l. Solishtiring: You must go — majburiyat. You must be tired — taxmin.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: must’ve, might’ve
scenes.say_native: Oldingi darslardagi bog‘lanish bu yerda juda kerak. Tez nutqda “have” zaiflashadi va /əv/ bo‘lib eshitiladi: “must’ve” /ˈmʌstəv/, “might’ve”, “could’ve”. “Have” dagi h tovushi tushib qoladi. Urg‘u modal fe’lga tushadi, “have” esa deyarli eshitilmaydi.
scenes.say: In fast speech, have becomes weak. Must have sounds like must've, /ˈmʌstəv/. Might have sounds like might've. Could have sounds like could've. The stress falls on the modal, and have almost disappears.
scenes.say_uz: Tez nutqda have zaiflashadi. Must have — must've. Might have — might've. Could have — could've. Urg'u modalga tushadi, have deyarli yo'qoladi.

scenes.title: Odatiy xatolar
board: ✓ She must have left. / must’ve left.
scenes.say_native: Uchta xato. Birinchisi: “mustn’t have” deb taxmin inkorini ifodalash. To‘g‘risi “can’t have”. Ikkinchisi: yozuvda “must of”, chunki “must’ve” tovushi “of” ga o‘xshaydi. Lekin to‘g‘risi “must have” yoki “must’ve”. Uchinchisi: “must has”. Modal fe’ldan keyin har doim “have” turadi, hech qachon “has” emas, chunki modal fe’llar -s qabul qilmaydi.
scenes.say: Three mistakes. First, mustn't have for a negative deduction: say can't have. Second, writing must of: it should be must have, or must've. Third, must has: modal verbs never take an s, and after them we always use have.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta xato. Birinchi: inkor taxmin uchun can't have deng. Ikkinchi: must of emas, must have yoki must've. Uchinchi: must has emas, modal fe'llar s olmaydi.

scenes.title: Taxmin qiling
board: 1) The lights are off. They ___ (be) out.
2) She’s not answering. She ___ (hear) the phone.  (possible)
3) He studied all night. He ___ (be) exhausted.
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uch gapni to‘g‘ri shakl bilan to‘ldiring. Birinchi: chiroqlar o‘chiq, ular chiqib ketgan bo‘lsa kerak. Ikkinchi: u telefonga javob bermayapti, eshitmagan bo‘lishi mumkin. Uchinchi: u tun bo‘yi o‘qidi, juda charchagan bo‘lsa kerak. Har bir javobda kerakli darajani tanlang. Baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Complete each sentence with the best modal. The lights are off: they ... out. She isn't answering: she possibly ... the phone. He studied all night: he is almost certainly ... exhausted.
scenes.say_uz: Har gapni to‘ldiring. Chiroqlar o‘chiq: ular chiqib ketgan. U javob bermayapti: telefonni eshitmagan bo‘lishi mumkin. U tun bo‘yi o‘qidi: juda charchagan bo‘lsa kerak.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1) They must be out. / must have gone out.
2) She might not have heard the phone.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “They must be out” yoki “They must have gone out”, chunki chiroq o‘chiq, bu kuchli belgi. Ikkinchi: “She might not have heard the phone”, ehtimol, shuning uchun might. Uchinchi: “He must be exhausted”, chunki sabab aniq. Qaysi modal tanlanganini sababi bilan tushuntirib bera olsangiz, mavzuni o‘zlashtirgansiz.
scenes.say: Answers. They must be out, or, they must have gone out. She might not have heard the phone. He must be exhausted. The choice depends on how strong the evidence is.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar. Ular chiqib ketgan bo'lsa kerak. U telefonni eshitmagan bo'lishi mumkin. U juda charchagan bo'lsa kerak. Tanlov dalil kuchiga bog'liq.

scenes.title: Tinglang: yo‘qolgan hamkasb
board: A: Where’s Dan? His laptop is here.
B: He must have gone for lunch.
A: He can’t have. His coat’s on the chair.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi dialog. Ikki hamkasb Dan qayerdaligini taxmin qilmoqda. Tinglang va qaysi taxmin kuchli, qaysi biri rad etilganini va nima uchun, aniqlang.
scenes.say: A: Where's Dan? His laptop is still here. B: He must have gone for lunch. A: He can't have. His coat is on the chair, and it's freezing outside. B: Then he might be in a meeting. A: Possibly. Or he could have popped out to the printer. B: Let's check. He's bound to be back soon.
scenes.say_uz: A: Dan qani? Noutbuki shu yerda. B: Tushlikka ketgan bo'lsa kerak. A: Ketgan bo'lishi mumkin emas. Paltosi stulda, tashqarida sovuq. B: Unda yig'ilishda bo'lishi mumkin. A: Ehtimol. Yoki printerga chiqqandir. B: Tekshiramiz. U tez qaytishi aniq.

scenes.title: Dialogni tekshiring
board: 1) Which guess does A reject? Why?
scenes.say_native: Uch savol. Birinchi: A qaysi taxminni rad etadi va nima uchun? Ikkinchi: ikkita mumkin bo‘lgan imkoniyatni ayting. Uchinchi: qaysi ibora kelajak haqida ishonchli bashorat beradi? Javobni o‘zingiz ayting.
scenes.say: Three questions. Which guess does A reject, and why? Name two possibilities. Which phrase predicts the future with confidence?
scenes.say_uz: Uch savol. A qaysi taxminni rad etadi va nima uchun? Ikki imkoniyatni ayting. Qaysi ibora kelajakni ishonch bilan bashorat qiladi?

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
board: 1) He can’t have gone: coat on chair
2) might be in a meeting / could have popped out
3) He’s bound to be back soon.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Bir: A “He can’t have” deydi, chunki paltosi stulda va tashqarida sovuq. Dalil aniq. Ikki: “He might be in a meeting” va “He could have popped out to the printer”. Uch: “He’s bound to be back soon” — albatta tez qaytadi. “Bound to” haqida endi alohida gaplashamiz.
scenes.say: Answers. A rejects the lunch idea with can't have, because the coat is on the chair. The possibilities are a meeting and a trip to the printer. He's bound to be back soon is the confident prediction.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar. A tushlik taxminini rad etadi, chunki palto stulda. Imkoniyatlar: yig'ilish va printer. He's bound to be back soon — ishonchli bashorat.

scenes.title: Probably, definitely, perhaps

examples.t: She’ll probably be late.
They definitely won’t come.
Maybe it will rain.

scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi mavzu. Ehtimol ma’nosidagi ravishlar. “Definitely” va “certainly” — aniq. “Probably” — katta ehtimol. “Possibly”, “perhaps”, “maybe” — kichikroq ehtimol. So‘z tartibi muhim: bu ravishlar “will” va “be” dan keyin turadi: “She’ll probably be late”.
scenes.say: Adverbs show probability. Definitely and certainly are the strongest. Probably is high. Possibly, perhaps and maybe are lower. Position matters: She'll probably be late. But before a negative: They definitely won't come. Maybe and perhaps usually start the sentence.
scenes.say_uz: Ravishlar ehtimolni ko'rsatadi. Definitely va certainly eng kuchli. Probably yuqori. Possibly, perhaps, maybe pastroq. O'rni muhim: will dan keyin, lekin inkorda won't dan oldin. Maybe va perhaps odatda gap boshida.

scenes.title: Likely, unlikely, bound to

examples.t: She is likely to win.
It’s unlikely to snow today.
He’s bound to be nervous.

scenes.say_native: Sifatlar bilan ham ehtimol bildiriladi. “Be likely to” — ehtimoli katta. “Be unlikely to” — ehtimoldan yiroq. “Be bound to” — deyarli aniq, albatta shunday bo‘ladi, ya’ni “must” ga yaqin lekin kelajak va umumiy kutilma uchun. “Be sure to” va “be certain to” ham shu darajada.
scenes.say: Adjectives work too. She is likely to win. It's unlikely to snow today. He's bound to be nervous, which means it is almost certain. After all of these, use to plus the base verb. You can also say, It's likely that she will win.
scenes.say_uz: Sifatlar ham ishlaydi. U g'olib bo'lishi ehtimoli katta. Bugun qor yog'ishi ehtimoldan yiroq. U albatta hayajonlanadi. Hammasidan keyin to va fe'l. Yoki: It's likely that she will win.

scenes.title: Ehtimol ifodalardagi xatolar
board: ✗ He will probably not to come.
✗ It is probably that he is late.
✓ It is probable that he is late.
scenes.say_native: Uchta xato. Birinchi: kelajak taxmini uchun “must” ishlatish. “It must rain tomorrow” noto‘g‘ri, chunki “must” hozirgi va o‘tgan haqidagi xulosa uchun. Kelajak uchun “will probably” yoki “is bound to”. Ikkinchi: “probably not to come”. Fe’lni bo‘sh holda ishlating: “probably won’t come”.
scenes.say: Common errors. Must is not used for predictions: It will probably rain tomorrow. Don't add to after won't. And probably is an adverb, so we say, It is probable that he is late, or, He is probably late.
scenes.say_uz: Odatiy xatolar. Must bashorat uchun emas: yomg'ir ehtimol yog'adi. Won't dan keyin to qo'shmang. Probably ravish, shuning uchun: It is probable that, yoki He is probably late.

scenes.title: Ehtimolni almashtiring
board: 1) I’m almost sure she will pass. (bound to)
2) It’s not very likely that he’ll call. (unlikely to)
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Gaplarni qavsdagi tuzilma bilan qayta yozing. Birinchi: “I’m almost sure she will pass” — “bound to” bilan. Ikkinchi: “It’s not very likely that he’ll call” — “unlikely to” bilan. Uchinchi: “Perhaps they’ll win” — “might” bilan. Ma’no o‘zgarmasin.
scenes.say: Rewrite each sentence with the structure in brackets. I'm almost sure she will pass, using bound to. It's not very likely that he'll call, using unlikely to. Perhaps they'll win, using might.
scenes.say_uz: Har gapni qavsdagi tuzilma bilan qayta yozing. Menimcha u albatta o'tadi. U qo'ng'iroq qilishi ehtimoldan yiroq. Ehtimol, ular yutishadi.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “She’s bound to pass”. Ikkinchi: “He’s unlikely to call”. Uchinchi: “They might win”. Ko‘rdingizmi, ma’no saqlandi, faqat tuzilma o‘zgardi. Bunday almashtirish yozma va og‘zaki nutqda takrorlanishdan qutqaradi, ayniqsa imtihonlarda baholanadi.
scenes.say: Answers. She's bound to pass. He's unlikely to call. They might win. The meaning stays the same while the structure changes, which gives your speech variety.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar. U albatta o'tadi. U qo'ng'iroq qilishi ehtimoldan yiroq. Ular yutishi mumkin. Ma'no saqlandi, tuzilma o'zgardi, nutq rang-barang bo'ladi.

scenes.title: Dalildan xulosa chiqarish
board: The lights are on, so they must be home.
His shoes are wet; it must have rained.

examples.t: The streets are wet. It must have rained.
examples.uz: Ko‘chalar nam. Yomg‘ir yoqqan bo‘lsa kerak.

examples.t: She’s wearing a ring. She must be married.
examples.uz: U uzuk taqqan. Turmush qurgan bo‘lsa kerak.

scenes.say_native: Uchinchi mavzu: deduction, ya’ni dalildan xulosa chiqarish. Bu detektiv kabi fikrlash: avval dalil, keyin xulosa. “The streets are wet. It must have rained.” Dalil — ko‘chalar nam, xulosa — yomg‘ir yoqqan. Dalil kuchli bo‘lsa “must” yoki “can’t”, zaif bo‘lsa “might” yoki “could”.
scenes.say: Deduction means reasoning from evidence, like a detective. The streets are wet, so it must have rained. She's wearing a ring, so she must be married. Strong evidence gives must or can't. Weak evidence gives might or could.
scenes.say_uz: Deduksiya — dalildan fikr yuritish, detektivdek. Ko'chalar nam, demak yomg'ir yoqqan bo'lsa kerak. U uzuk taqqan, turmush qurgan bo'lsa kerak. Kuchli dalil — must yoki can't. Zaif dalil — might yoki could.

scenes.title: Looks like, seems, appears
board: It seems that... / He seems to be...

examples.t: It looks as if it’s going to rain.
He seems to be upset.

scenes.say_native: Taxminni modal fe’lsiz ham bildirish mumkin. “It looks as if” yoki “It looks like” — ko‘rinishidan shunday. “He seems to be upset” — u xafa bo‘lganga o‘xshaydi. “It appears that” rasmiyroq, ko‘proq yozma nutqda. Bu so‘zlar sezgi organlari bilan olingan belgiga tayanadi, shuning uchun ular dalil bor ekanini ham ko‘rsatadi.
scenes.say: You can speculate without modals. It looks as if it's going to rain. He seems to be upset. It appears that the meeting has been cancelled, which is more formal. These verbs rely on what we see or hear.
scenes.say_uz: Modalsiz ham taxmin qilsa bo'ladi. Yomg'ir yog'adiganga o'xshaydi. U xafa bo'lganga o'xshaydi. Uchrashuv bekor qilinganga o'xshaydi, bu rasmiyroq. Bu fe'llar ko'rgan yoki eshitganimizga tayanadi.

scenes.title: Kelajak va dalil
board: They should be here by six.

examples.t: Look at those clouds. It’s going to rain.
They should be here by six.
examples.uz: Ular oltigacha shu yerda bo‘lishi kerak.

scenes.say_native: Kelajak haqida dalilga asoslangan bashorat uchun “be going to” ishlatiladi: “Look at those clouds. It’s going to rain”. Bulutlar — hozirgi dalil. Oddiy kutilma uchun “should”: “They should be here by six” — ular oltigacha kelishi kerak, ya’ni men shunday kutyapman. Bu “majburiy” degani emas.
scenes.say: For predictions based on present evidence, use be going to: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain. For a reasonable expectation, use should: They should be here by six. This is not an obligation. It simply means I expect it.
scenes.say_uz: Hozirgi dalilga asoslangan bashorat uchun be going to: bulutlarga qarang, yomg'ir yog'adi. Oqilona kutilma uchun should: ular oltigacha kelishi kerak. Bu majburiyat emas, kutilma.

scenes.title: Dalilga asoslanib gapiring
board: 1) A man has a tan and a suitcase.
2) The office is dark and the door is locked.
3) The phone is ringing, nobody answers.
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uch vaziyat uchun dalildan xulosa chiqaring. Birinchi: erkak qoraygan va qo‘lida chamadon. Ikkinchi: ofis qorong‘i va eshik qulflangan. Uchinchi: telefon jiringlayapti, hech kim ko‘tarmayapti. Har biri uchun ikki xulosa ayting: kuchli va kuchsiz.
scenes.say: Three situations. Make a strong and a weak deduction for each. A man has a tan and a suitcase. The office is dark and the door is locked. A phone is ringing and nobody answers.
scenes.say_uz: Uch vaziyat. Har biri uchun kuchli va kuchsiz xulosa ayting. Erkak qoraygan va chamadonli. Ofis qorong'i va qulflangan. Telefon jiringlayapti, hech kim ko'tarmayapti.

scenes.title: Namunaviy javoblar
board: 1) He must have been on holiday. He might have just landed.
2) Everyone must have gone home. It could be a bank holiday.
3) They must be out. They might not have heard it.
scenes.say_native: Namunalar. Birinchi: “He must have been on holiday”, kuchli. “He might have just landed”, kuchsiz. Ikkinchi: “Everyone must have gone home”, “It could be a bank holiday”. Uchinchi: “They must be out”, “They might not have heard it”. Sizning javoblaringiz boshqacha bo‘lishi mumkin, muhimi dalil va modal darajasi mos kelsin.
scenes.say: Model answers. He must have been on holiday. He might have just landed. Everyone must have gone home. It could be a bank holiday. They must be out. They might not have heard it. Match your modal to the strength of the evidence.
scenes.say_uz: Namunalar. U ta'tilda bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak. Endigina qo'nishi mumkin. Hamma uyga ketgan bo'lsa kerak. Bayram kuni bo'lishi mumkin. Ular chiqib ketgan. Eshitmagan bo'lishi mumkin. Modalni dalil kuchiga moslang.

scenes.title: Tinglang: kechikkan do‘st
board: Mia: Ben’s late. It isn’t like him.
Leo: He must have got stuck in traffic.
Mia: He can’t have. He cycles.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog. Mia va Leo kechikayotgan do‘stini kutmoqda. Ular har xil darajadagi taxminlar aytadi. Tinglang va har bir taxmin qanchalik ishonchli ekanini baholang.
scenes.say: Mia: Ben's twenty minutes late. It isn't like him. Leo: He must have got stuck in traffic. Mia: He can't have. He cycles everywhere. Leo: True. Then he may have forgotten. Mia: I doubt it. I'd say he's probably lost his phone. Leo: Look, that's him. He's running. He looks exhausted. Mia: Well, he's bound to have an excuse.
scenes.say_uz: Mia: Ben yigirma daqiqa kechikdi. Bu unga o'xshamaydi. Leo: Tirbandlikda qolgan bo'lsa kerak. Mia: Bo'lishi mumkin emas, u hamma yerga velosipedda boradi. Leo: To'g'ri. Unda unutgan bo'lishi mumkin. Mia: Shubhali. Menimcha, telefonini yo'qotgan. Leo: Qarang, o'sha! Yugurib kelyapti, charchaganga o'xshaydi. Mia: Uning bahonasi albatta bor.

scenes.title: Ishonch darajasini toping
scenes.say_native: Uchta savol. Birinchi: nima uchun tirbandlik taxmini rad etildi? Ikkinchi: qaysi taxmin eng kuchsiz? Uchinchi: qaysi ibora shubha bildiradi? Dialogni xotirangizdan tiklab ayting.
scenes.say: Three questions. Why is stuck in traffic rejected? Which guess is the weakest? Which phrase shows doubt?
scenes.say_uz: Uch savol. Nega tirbandlik rad etildi? Qaysi taxmin eng kuchsiz? Qaysi ibora shubha bildiradi?

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Bir: Mia “He can’t have” dedi, chunki Ben hamma joyga velosipedda boradi, ya’ni tirbandlik unga ta’sir qilmaydi. Ikki: “He may have forgotten” — eng kuchsiz taxmin, Mia uni ham shubha bilan rad etdi. Uch: “I doubt it” — menimcha unday emas. Miyaning “I’d say he’s probably…” iborasi ham yumshoq, ammo ishonchli taxmin.
scenes.say: Answers. Mia rejects traffic with can't have, because Ben cycles everywhere. He may have forgotten is the weakest guess. I doubt it expresses doubt. And I'd say he's probably lost his phone is a soft but confident guess.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar. Mia tirbandlikni rad etadi, chunki Ben velosipedda boradi. Unutgan bo'lishi mumkin — eng kuchsiz taxmin. I doubt it shubha bildiradi. I'd say he's probably... yumshoq, ammo ishonchli taxmin.

scenes.title: Ishonch shkalasi
scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi mavzu: ishonch darajalari. Tasavvur qiling, bu shkala. Yuqorida “definitely” va “must”. Keyin “bound to” va “certain to”. O‘rtada “probably”, “likely”, “should”. Pastroqda “may”, “might”, “could”. Undan pastda “unlikely”. Eng pastda “can’t” va “definitely not”. Raqamlar taxminiy, lekin tartib to‘g‘ri.
scenes.say: Think of certainty as a scale. At the top, definitely and must. Then bound to and certain to. In the middle, probably, likely and should. Lower down, may, might and could. Then unlikely. At the bottom, can't and definitely not. Ask yourself how sure you are, then choose the word.
scenes.say_uz: Ishonchni shkala deb tasavvur qiling. Yuqorida definitely va must. Keyin bound to. O'rtada probably, likely, should. Pastroqda may, might, could. Undan pastda unlikely. Eng pastda can't. O'zingizdan so'rang: qanchalik ishonaman? Keyin so'z tanlang.

scenes.title: Ehtiyotkor ifodalar

examples.t: There’s a good chance that she’ll accept.
I wouldn’t be surprised if he resigned.

scenes.say_native: B2 darajasida bir xil modal fe’llar yetmaydi. “I’d say” — menimcha. “There’s a good chance that” — ehtimol yuqori. “There’s a slim chance” — imkoniyat juda kam. “I wouldn’t be surprised if” — agar shunday bo‘lsa ajablanmasdim, ya’ni ehtimol katta. “It’s just possible that” — ehtimol, lekin kam.
scenes.say: At B2 you need more than modals. I'd say she'll accept. There's a good chance that she'll accept. There's a slim chance that she'll refuse. I wouldn't be surprised if he resigned.
scenes.say_uz: B2 da modal fe'llardan boshqa vositalar kerak. Menimcha, u qabul qiladi. Qabul qilish ehtimoli yuqori. Rad etish ehtimoli juda kam. U iste'foga chiqsa ajablanmasdim.

scenes.title: Norasmiy va rasmiy
board: Formal: It is likely that..., It seems probable that...

examples.t: I bet she’s forgotten.
It seems probable that prices will rise.

scenes.say_native: Yana bir nuqta — uslub. Do‘stlar orasida “I bet she’s forgotten” — garov bog‘laman, unutgan. “I reckon” — menimcha, norasmiy, ayniqsa Britaniyada. Neytral: “I think”, “I suppose”. Rasmiy yozuvda: “It is likely that”, “It seems probable that”. Imtihon yozish topshirig‘ida rasmiy shakl, suhbatda norasmiy shakl kerak.
scenes.say: Style matters. With friends: I bet she's forgotten. I reckon it will be fine. Neutral: I think, I suppose. Formal writing: It is likely that, It seems probable that prices will rise. Choose the register that suits your reader.
scenes.say_uz: Uslub muhim. Do'stlar bilan: garov bog'layman, unutgan. Neytral: I think. Rasmiy yozuvda: It is likely that, It seems probable that. O'quvchingizga mos uslubni tanlang.

scenes.title: Taxminga qisqa javoblar
board: Do you think he’ll come? — Probably.
— I suppose so. / I’m not sure.

examples.t: Will she pass? — She’s bound to.
Is he angry? — I doubt it.

scenes.say_native: Suhbatda taxminga ko‘pincha qisqa javob beriladi. “Probably” — ehtimol. “He might” — mumkin. “I doubt it” — shubhali. “I suppose so” — shekilli, shunday. “Not likely” — ehtimoldan yiroq. “Definitely not” — aniq yo‘q. Bunday qisqa javoblar nutqingizni tabiiy qiladi va to‘liq gap tuzish shart emas.
scenes.say: In conversation we often answer with short phrases. Probably. He might. I doubt it. I suppose so. Not likely. Definitely not. Will she pass? She's bound to. Is he angry? I doubt it.
scenes.say_uz: Suhbatda qisqa javoblar ishlatiladi. Ehtimol. Mumkin. Shubhali. Shekilli. Ehtimoldan yiroq. Aniq yo‘q. U o‘tadimi? Albatta. U g‘azablanganmi? Shubhali.

scenes.title: Ortiqcha ishonch
board: ✗ He must be there. (sure? no evidence)
✓ Maybe he’ll come. / He may come.
scenes.say_native: Ikki xato. Birinchi: dalil bo‘lmasa, “must” ishlatish. Agar siz faqat o‘ylayotgan bo‘lsangiz, “might” yoki “could” deng. Aks holda gapingiz juda ishonchli eshitiladi va noto‘g‘ri bo‘lsa, noqulay. Ikkinchi: “maybe” bilan “may” ni birga ishlatish. “Maybe he may come” keraksiz takror.
scenes.say: Two errors. First, using must without evidence. If you are only guessing, say might or could. Second, doubling up: Maybe he may come repeats the idea. Say Maybe he'll come, or He may come. Remember, maybe is one word, an adverb, while may be is a verb phrase.
scenes.say_uz: Ikki xato. Birinchi: dalilsiz must. Faqat o'ylasangiz, might yoki could. Ikkinchi: Maybe he may come takror. Yoki Maybe he'll come, yoki He may come. Maybe — bitta so'z, ravish; may be — fe'l.

scenes.title: Qisqa javob bering
board: 2) Is the shop open on Sunday? (30%)
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uchta savolga qavsdagi ishonchga mos qisqa javob bering. Birinchi: ertaga yomg‘ir yog‘adimi, to‘qson foiz ishonch. Ikkinchi: do‘kon yakshanba kuni ochiqmi, o‘ttiz foiz. Uchinchi: u yolg‘on gapirdimi, aniq yo‘q deb bilasiz.
scenes.say: Answer with a short phrase that matches your certainty. Will it rain tomorrow? Ninety per cent sure. Is the shop open on Sunday? Thirty per cent. Did he lie? You are sure he didn't.
scenes.say_uz: Ishonchingizga mos qisqa javob bering. Ertaga yomg‘ir yog‘adimi? To‘qson foiz. Do‘kon yakshanba ochiqmi? O‘ttiz foiz. U yolg‘on gapirdimi? Aniq yo‘q.

scenes.title: Qisqa javob namunalari
board: 2) It might be. / I doubt it.
scenes.say_native: Namunalar. Birinchi: “It’s bound to” yoki “Probably”. Ikkinchi, o‘ttiz foiz uchun: “It might be” yoki “I doubt it”. Uchinchi: “He can’t have” yoki “Definitely not”. Ko‘rdingizmi, har bir javob ishonch darajasiga mos keldi. Aynan shu moslik taxmin qilishning mohiyati.
scenes.say: Model answers. It's bound to, or, Probably. It might be, or, I doubt it. He can't have, or, Definitely not. Each answer matches the level of certainty.
scenes.say_uz: Namunalar. Albatta yog‘adi. Ochiq bo‘lishi mumkin, yoki shubhali. Yolg‘on gapirgan bo‘lishi mumkin emas. Har javob ishonch darajasiga mos.

scenes.title: Tartiblang
scenes.say_native: Mashq. To‘rtta gapni qor yog‘adi degan ishonchning eng kuchlisidan eng kuchsizigacha tartiblang. A: “It might snow”. B: “It’s bound to snow”. C: “It’s unlikely to snow”. D: “It can’t snow”. Harflar ketma-ketligini ayting.
scenes.say: Put the four sentences in order, from the strongest belief that it will snow, to the weakest. A, It might snow. B, It's bound to snow. C, It's unlikely to snow. D, It can't snow.
scenes.say_uz: To'rt gapni qor yog'adi degan ishonchning eng kuchlisidan eng kuchsizigacha tartiblang. A, qor yog'ishi mumkin. B, albatta yog'adi. C, yog'ishi ehtimoldan yiroq. D, yog'ishi mumkin emas.

scenes.title: To‘g‘ri tartib
scenes.say_native: Javob: B, A, C, D. Eng kuchli “bound to snow”, undan keyin “might snow”, keyin “unlikely”, eng oxirida “can’t snow”, chunki u qor yog‘ishini butunlay inkor etadi. Bu mashq shuni ko‘rsatadi: darajani to‘g‘ri tanlash lug‘atni bilishdan ham muhimroq. Bir xil mavzuda to‘rt xil fikr bildira olasiz.
scenes.say: The order is B, A, C, D. Bound to snow is the strongest. Might snow is possible. Unlikely to snow is low. Can't snow rejects it completely. Choosing the right degree matters as much as knowing the words.
scenes.say_uz: Tartib: B, A, C, D. Bound to snow eng kuchli. Might snow mumkin. Unlikely to snow past. Can't snow butunlay inkor. To'g'ri daraja lug'atdek muhim.

scenes.title: Rasmlar uchun tayyorlanish
board: Picture 1: an empty coffee cup and a coat on a chair
Picture 2: a crowded station, a delayed train
Plan: evidence → strong guess → weak guess
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy topshiriq uchun tayyorlaning. Tasavvur qiling: birinchi rasmda bo‘sh kofe finjoni va stulda palto. Ikkinchisida gavjum vokzal va kechikayotgan poyezd. Har biri uchun reja: dalil, kuchli taxmin, kuchsiz taxmin. Hozir ikkita jumla o‘ylab oling.
scenes.say: Prepare for your final task. Picture one: an empty coffee cup and a coat on a chair. Picture two: a crowded station and a delayed train. For each, plan the evidence, one strong guess and one weak guess.
scenes.say_uz: Yakuniy topshiriqqa tayyorlaning. Bir: bo'sh finjon va stulda palto. Ikki: gavjum vokzal va kechikkan poyezd. Har biri uchun dalil, kuchli va kuchsiz taxmin.

scenes.title: Namunaviy taxminlar
board: Picture 1: Someone must have just left. They might be back soon.
Picture 2: There must have been a problem on the line. Passengers are bound to be annoyed.
scenes.say_native: Namuna. Birinchi rasm: “Someone must have just left, because the coat is still here. They might be coming back soon.” Ikkinchi rasm: “There must have been a problem on the line. The passengers look tired, so they have probably been waiting a while. They’re bound to be annoyed.” Har birida dalil, kuchli xulosa va ehtimoliy davomi bor.
scenes.say: A model answer. Someone must have just left, because the coat is still here. They might be coming back soon. And: There must have been a problem on the line. The passengers have probably been waiting a while. They're bound to be annoyed.
scenes.say_uz: Namuna. Kimdir hozirgina ketgan bo'lsa kerak, chunki palto shu yerda. Tez qaytishi mumkin. Liniyada muammo bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak. Yo'lovchilar ancha kutgan bo'lsa kerak. Ular albatta g'azablangan.

scenes.title: Oltita vaziyat
board: Use: must, might, can’t, probably, bound to.
scenes.say_native: Endi sizning navbatingiz. O‘zingiz tanlagan oltita rasm yoki vaziyat haqida taxmin qiling: ko‘chadagi odam, bo‘sh sinf, yomg‘irli osmon, kechikkan do‘st, qulflangan eshik, ko‘p odamli kafe. Har biri uchun kamida bitta kuchli va bitta kuchsiz taxmin ayting va dalilni tushuntiring.
scenes.say: Your turn. Speculate about six pictures or situations: a person in the street, an empty classroom, a rainy sky, a late friend, a locked door, a crowded café. Give one strong and one weak guess for each, with evidence.
scenes.say_uz: Navbat sizda. Olti vaziyat haqida taxmin qiling: ko'chadagi odam, bo'sh sinf, yomg'irli osmon, kechikkan do'st, qulflangan eshik, gavjum kafe. Har biri uchun kuchli va kuchsiz taxmin va dalil.

scenes.title: O‘zingizni tekshiring
board: ☐ probably / bound to for the future
scenes.say_native: Tekshirib ko‘ring. Kuchli dalilda “must” yoki “can’t” ishlatdingizmi? Zaif dalilda “might” yoki “could”? O‘tmish uchun “have” va uchinchi shaklni qo‘lladingizmi? Kelajak uchun “probably” yoki “bound to”? Va eng muhimi, “mustn’t have” yoki “must of” kabi xatolardan qochdingizmi? Bir joyda adashgan bo‘lsangiz, o‘sha qismga qaytib, yana urinib ko‘ring.
scenes.say: Check yourself. Did you use must or can't for strong evidence, and might or could for weak evidence? Did you use have plus a past participle for the past? Probably or bound to for the future? And did you avoid mustn't have and must of?
scenes.say_uz: O'zingizni tekshiring. Kuchli dalilda must yoki can't, zaifida might yoki could? O'tmish uchun have va uchinchi shakl? Kelajak uchun probably yoki bound to? Mustn't have va must of dan qochdingizmi?

scenes.title: Dars xulosasi
board: must have / might have / can’t have + V3
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Birinchi: “must have”, “might have”, “can’t have” va uchinchi shakl bilan o‘tmishni taxmin qilamiz. Ikkinchi: “probably”, “likely to”, “bound to” kelajak va hozir ehtimolini bildiradi. Uchinchi: dalildan xulosa chiqaramiz. To‘rtinchi: ishonch darajasini shkaladan tanlaymiz. Bularning hammasi aniq ishonch bilan gapirishga yordam beradi.
scenes.say: Let's recap. Must have, might have and can't have plus a past participle speculate about the past. Probably, likely to and bound to express probability. We reason from evidence, and we choose the degree of certainty carefully.
scenes.say_uz: Takrorlaymiz. Must have, might have, can't have va uchinchi shakl o'tmishni taxmin qiladi. Probably, likely to, bound to ehtimolni bildiradi. Dalildan xulosa chiqaramiz va ishonch darajasini ehtiyotkorlik bilan tanlaymiz.

scenes.title: Esda tuting: xatolar
board: ✗ It must rain → ✓ It will probably rain
✗ Maybe he may → ✓ Maybe he will
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta xatoni qaytaramiz. “Mustn’t have” emas, “can’t have”. “Must of” emas, “must have” yoki “must’ve”. Kelajak uchun “must” emas, “will probably” yoki “is bound to”. “Maybe he may” emas, “maybe he will” yoki “he may”. Bu to‘rttasini yodlab olsangiz, taxmin ifodalashdagi asosiy xatolarning ko‘pi yo‘qoladi.
scenes.say: Four fixes. Not mustn't have, but can't have. Not must of, but must have. Not It must rain, but It will probably rain. Not Maybe he may, but Maybe he will, or, He may.
scenes.say_uz: To'rt tuzatish. Mustn't have emas, can't have. Must of emas, must have. It must rain emas, will probably rain. Maybe he may emas, maybe he will yoki he may.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Homework: speculate about 6 pictures or situations
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifangiz: oltita rasm yoki vaziyat haqida taxmin qiling. Har biri uchun ikkita gap: bitta kuchli va bitta kuchsiz taxmin, dalil bilan. Ovozingizni yozib oling. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: kamida to‘rt xil tuzilma ishlating, va bir marta ham “mustn’t have” yoki “must of” demang. Keyingi darsda media, reklama va yangiliklar haqida gaplashamiz.
scenes.say: Homework: speculate about six pictures or situations. Give two sentences each, one strong guess and one weak guess, with evidence. Record yourself, and use at least four different structures. Next time we will talk about media, advertising and news.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifasi: olti rasm yoki vaziyat haqida taxmin qiling. Har biri uchun ikki gap: kuchli va kuchsiz taxmin, dalil bilan. Ovozingizni yozing, kamida to'rt xil tuzilma ishlating. Keyingi darsda media, reklama va yangiliklar.

homework_uz: Oltita rasm yoki vaziyat haqida taxmin qiling: har biri uchun bitta kuchli va bitta kuchsiz taxmin, dalil bilan. Ovozingizni yozib oling. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: kamida to‘rt xil tuzilma va bitta ham “mustn’t have” yoki “must of” xatosi bo‘lmasin.

quiz.q: The streets are wet. It ___ rained.
quiz.why_uz: Dalil kuchli, o‘tmish uchun must have + V3. Must of va must has xato.

quiz.q: She isn't here. She ___ the message. (I'm sure she didn't)
quiz.why_uz: Inkor xulosa uchun can't have, mustn't have emas.

options: It is probably that rain tomorrow.
quiz.why_uz: Kelajak bashorati: will probably; must kelajak uchun emas.

quiz.q: He's ___ be late; he always is.
Which is the weakest belief that it will happen?

quiz.why_uz: Might not have — ehtimol; can't have — aniq.

quiz.q: Which is a deduction from evidence?
options: She's wearing a ring, so she must be married.
quiz.why_uz: Bu yerda must taxmin ma'nosida; boshqalar majburiyat.
Maybe he'll come yoki He may come; ikkalasini aralashtirmang.
